listing.name: Gunstar Heroes (gunstars)
listing.summary: A native engine for Gunstar Heroes using your own original cartridge data.

steps.title: Choose your original cartridge dump
steps.instruction: On first Play, select your own 1 MiB USA Gunstar Heroes cartridge dump in the file browser. Keep the ROM outside the player folder.

steps.title: Start the Windows or Linux player
steps.instruction: The v0.2.2 Windows x64 ZIP runs gunstar.exe. The Linux x86-64 tar.gz runs gunstar and requires SDL2 and a system with glibc 2.28 or later. Keep each package together.

warnings: Back up settings.ini, states, screenshots, videos and any custom destinations with the game closed. On Windows and Linux these paths default to the player working directory. Keep your original ROM and the compatible old player separately.

references.title: Open the universal Mac app
references.instruction: Unzip the v0.2.2 macos-universal ZIP and keep gunstars.app intact. The Intel and Apple silicon app needs macOS 11 or later. Open it in Finder for the profile under ~/Library/Application Support/gunstars. A direct Terminal launch uses its working directory. Maintain this copy outside Portcove.

presentation.manual_preparation: On Play, use the upstream in-process file browser to select your own Gunstar Heroes USA 1 MiB cartridge dump, or retain an established --rom argument. The selected engine checks size and CRC32 B813CF0D for compatibility; that is not Core cryptographic source authentication. Core does not acquire, copy or import the ROM. Keep it outside the engine directory and preserve it separately. The Windows player gunstar.exe and Linux player gunstar keeps settings.ini, states (including slots/autosave and previews), screenshots and videos relative to its executable working directory; Core preserves these declared default paths across its engine maintenance. User-configured state/capture paths can point elsewhere and remain external, outside Core backup/removal. Retain every actual override location and compatible old runtime before changes; restore does not promise backward state compatibility. The Linux package needs SDL2 and glibc 2.28 or later. Mac setup is player-managed. Normal local play is offered; multiplayer/replay/GIF/gameplay claims remain upstream-only. Existing external registrations keep their own replacement owner.
